transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-04-29
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Li (Redwood SE), Monica Reyes (Ledgerly CTO), Samir Patel (Ledgerly ML Eng), Jenna Lowe (Product), Carlos Vega (Infra)

Summary: Quick sync on cache hit-rate improvements; look at what changed after TTL/segmentation tuning; decide next benchmarking steps.

[00:00] Ethan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly caching sync for the Ledgerly POC. real quick, who all do we have?
[00:08] Monica Reyes: Monica here, Samir's on, Jenna and Carlos as well.
[00:11] Samir Patel: yep, Samir.
[00:13] Ethan Park: great. Sofia and I will run through the numbers we pushed overnight. we changed the prefix policy and bumped kv cache TTLs.
[00:22] Sofia Li: yeah quick note, the KV cash - kv cash, sorry - the KV cache hit rate jumped after we moved to the segmented TTLs and introduced a small LRU bias.
[00:31] Jenna Lowe: can you give the baseline and new numbers?
[00:34] Sofia Li: baseline prefix cache hit rate was about 12%, kv was 32% across the test set. after tuning, prefix is at ~46% and KV at ~58% for the 24-hour window in staging.
[00:50] Carlos Vega: those are pretty big lifts, curiosity: what's the cost impact (memory/cost tradeoff)?
[00:55] Sofia Li: good call. we increased mem pressure by about 18% because we hold more prefix segments per shard. cost uplift on the GPU nodes is small relative to token savings - our estimation is roughly 7-9% token cost reduction in production when these hit rates hold.
[01:12] Monica Reyes: hmm, what about cold-starts? we still see some latency spikes in the morning traffic.
[01:17] Ethan Park: yeah cold starts are expected. we recommended a warm-start job; Sofia, did you try the warm-start prefetch?
[01:22] Sofia Li: yes we ran a 30-minute warm-start in staging that prefetches popular prefixes; it smoothed p95 by ~120ms on the sample.
[01:30] Samir Patel: can you explain the prefix segmentation? I think I misread the doc last week.
[01:34] Sofia Li: sure. instead of storing the whole prompt context as one key, we break into prefix buckets - short prompts, medium, long - that gives higher reuse because many of Ledgerly's requests share the initial 40-120 token template. it increases collisions a bit but improves reuse overall.
[01:49] Jenna Lowe: is there any risk of returning stale cached KV entries for dynamic fields? like session-specific tokens?
[01:55] Ethan Park: great point - we rely on the prompt canonicalization layer to strip ephemeral fields (session ids, timestamps) before hitting the cache. we saw a couple misses where the client didn't canonicalize, Samir i think you fixed one of those generator pipelines?
[02:06] Samir Patel: yep, corrected the templating for two endpoints. we also added a hash salt to avoid cross-user leakage.
[02:12] Carlos Vega: on eviction, what's the policy? LRU? TTL? hybrid?
[02:16] Sofia Li: hybrid. TTL primary per-segment (shorter TTL for short templates), plus LRU to recover space. we tuned percentiles so high-freq keys stay in memory.
[02:24] Monica Reyes: any tooling to estimate expected hit-rate before we deploy?
[02:28] Sofia Li: we have a synthetic simulator that replays a sample of your traffic against a proposed cache config. we ran it with 100k historical requests, that produced the 46%/58% numbers. we'll share the script and dashboard.
[02:40] Ethan Park: also note the numbers vary by time-window; 24-hour aggregation gives higher apparent rate because of repeated queries. rolling 1-hour hit rate is lower - around 30-35% after tuning.
[02:51] Jenna Lowe: that's important because our peak latency SLO is tight. how will this affect p95 under load?
[02:56] Sofia Li: with prefix hits we reduce generation tokens by about 60% for hit requests, which reduces backend compute. we measured p95 improvement in staging by ~80-120ms depending on model and sequence length.
[03:08] Samir Patel: what's the implication for dedicated vs hosted? if we go dedicated, do we still see same gains?
[03:13] Ethan Park: yes, the runtime is the same, but dedicated gives you ability to size memory/kv store to hit higher resident sets. hosted has shared resource limits so your effective resident set might be smaller unless you commit reserved capacity.
[03:25] Monica Reyes: say we want to push this to a pilot on dedicated, what does it cost/time wise?
[03:30] Ethan Park: we'd size a node pool with higher memory for KV, plus a small reserved slice. Sofia can prepare a cost estimate for both dedicated vs reserved-hosted burst.
[03:40] Sofia Li: I'll send a comparative spreadsheet; early estimate is dedicated +/- 12-18% higher infra but lower per-token over sustained traffic due to better cache residency.
[03:52] Jenna Lowe: any security concerns with caching? we need to keep PII out and ensure KMS logs are recorded.
[03:58] Ethan Park: caching only stores canonicalized prompt text and model KV states; PII should be removed by your canonicalization. we also support KMS encryption at rest and audit logs - we'll send the SOC2 checklist and the staging encryption keys flow.
[04:12] Monica Reyes: please send that - security will want to review.
[04:15] Ethan Park: will do.
[04:17] Sofia Li: next, prompt reuse strategy: we recommend centralizing common templates in your prompt library and tagging them so the canonicalizer can detect duplicates. small change in client side can boost reuse by 8-10% in our tests.
[04:30] Samir Patel: sounds easy. we can standardize endpoints and push to the template registry.
[04:33] Ethan Park: last bit, gotchas: watch out for long-tail prompts that create many unique keys - we suggest falling back to hashed-only caching for those to avoid explosion.
[04:42] Carlos Vega: on monitoring, can we get per-route hit rates and token savings?
[04:46] Sofia Li: yes - per-route dashboards are available; we'll add two charts: token savings and estimated $ savings.
[04:53] Jenna Lowe: ok let's recap.
[04:55] Ethan Park: recap: Ethan/Sofia will push TTL/eviction changes to staging; Sofia will share dashboard + warm-start script; Ledgerly runs 12k request benchmark and returns results; security doc and SOC2 checklist shared; follow-up next week.
[05:10] Monica Reyes: agreed. thanks all.
[05:13] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and the spreadsheet after.

End of transcript.
